Name a more iconic song for a movie ending… 

Cruel Intentions (1999) is a slick teen drama set in Manhattan’s wealthy world. Directed by Roger Kumble, it follows step siblings Sebastian and Kathryn, who play a dangerous game of seduction. Their target is an innocent girl, and things get messy as real feelings start to get in the way.

Full of sharp dialogue and drama, the movie shows the emptiness behind money and status. The young cast delivers memorable performances that make the twists and betrayals feel real.

More than just a steamy teen story, Cruel Intentions is about manipulation, desire, and what happens when people play with emotions they can’t control.

source_details.synopsis: Cruel Intentions is a 1999 American teen romantic drama film written and directed by Roger Kumble, and starring Ryan Phillippe, Sarah Michelle Gellar, Reese Witherspoon, and Selma Blair. The film, set in New York City among rich high schoolers, is a modern retelling of Pierre Choderlos de Laclos' 1782 novel Les Liaisons dangereuses. Initially a smaller-budget independent film, it was picked up by Columbia Pictures and widely released on March 5, 1999. Despite mixed critical reviews, the performances of Gellar, Phillippe, and Witherspoon were praised and the film grossed $76 million worldwide.
